newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Flat Australian bonds end looking for leads.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Flat Australian bonds end looking for leads.

text.p: *Australian bonds end basically flat after an uneventful day that saw them confined to narrow ranges.
*Market looking to offshore for leads next week, Greenspan's Senate committee apearance seen as the most important.
Australian bonds ended flat to slightly stronger after an uneventful day notable only for a lack of direction and drive, traders said.
Bonds spent the day in narrow ranges around their previous closes. March 10-year bond futures traded a 4.5 point range on the day, while the three year contract managed a six point band.
"It's very quiet and I'm just not quite sure what's going to change in the next couple of days," one trader said.
After opening slightly softer on the back of a weaker U.S. market, bonds nudged higher through the morning and held basically steady through the afternoon.
Even some early weakness in bills, as the chances of a near term easing narrowed, failed to develop through the day.
With December merchandise imports data on Monday the only major event scheduled for next week, near term leads will have to come from offshore, traders said.

While some direction could come from U.S. trade, production and capacity utilisation data later today, traders said the most important event would be Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments before the Senate committee next Tuesday.
Despite the lacklustre close to the week, bonds still finished around 10 points stronger across the curve on the week.

Despite lacklustre performance of local market, the flat to positive finish sees bonds outperform other countries. NZ bonds sold on disappointing inflation result, but the short end had recouped some of its initial losses. Curve contiues the flattening trend evident in the second half of the week.
